metadata.title: The Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 (SI 2004/1031)
metadata.edition: As amended, incl. SI 2025/538 (reg. 33 changes in force 28 Apr 2026) · Made 17 Mar 2004; in force 1 May 2004
metadata.legal_basis: Listed in the PV Info document catalog (UK Government); the official text governs.
metadata.applicability: See the official document for scope and applicability.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement: (1) A sponsor shall ensure that all relevant information about a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction which occurs during the course of a clinical trial in the United Kingdom and is fatal or life-threatening is reported as soon as possible to the licensing authority, and in any event no later than 7 days after the sponsor was first aware of the reaction.
candidates.context: (2) A sponsor shall ensure that within 8 days of a report in accordance with paragraph (1), any additional relevant information is sent to the licensing authority.

candidates.statement: (2) A sponsor shall ensure that within 8 days of a report in accordance with paragraph (1), any additional relevant information is sent to the licensing authority.
candidates.context: (1) A sponsor shall ensure that all relevant information about a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction which occurs during the course of a clinical trial in the United Kingdom and is fatal or life-threatening is reported as soon as possible to the licensing authority, and in any event no later than 7 days after the sponsor was first aware of the reaction. (3) A sponsor shall ensure that a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction which occurs during the course of a clinical trial in the United Kingdom, other than those referred to in paragraph (1), is reported as soon as possible to the licensing authority, and in any event no later than 15 days after the sponsor is first aware of the reaction.

candidates.statement: (3) A sponsor shall ensure that a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction which occurs during the course of a clinical trial in the United Kingdom, other than those referred to in paragraph (1), is reported as soon as possible to the licensing authority, and in any event no later than 15 days after the sponsor is first aware of the reaction.

candidates.statement: (4B) The sponsor shall report suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions to which paragraph (4A) applies to the licensing authority in accordance with the reporting requirements, including the time periods for such reporting, that are specified in the protocol.
